channel.title: Krunalkumar Shah — Blog
channel.description: Articles by Krunalkumar Shah on mentorship, careers, cybersecurity research, and automation — practical writing drawn from real work.

item.title: How I Vibe Coded This Website — And the Mechanism That Made It Hold
item.description: I did not hand-write most of this site. What made it hold was the mechanism around the prompting — the prompt as a specification, the reasoning kept in the repository, adversarial review passes, and a build that refuses to publish damage.

item.title: AI Driven, Human Assisted: The Default Just Inverted
item.description: Human driven, AI assisted was the safe arrangement for a decade, because the tool could not hold a plan. It can now — what the inversion changes, the four jobs a human keeps, and where AI driven is still the wrong default.

item.title: Types of Cyberattacks, Mapped: Causes, Defenses, and the CIA Triad
item.description: Six attack families, what each one breaks, why they keep working, and the prevention and mitigation that actually help — one practical map built on the CIA triad.

item.title: Security Compliance, Explained: GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOC 2, and More
item.description: A practical guide to security and privacy compliance — GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOX, ISO/IEC 27001, and SOC 2 — what each one is, who it binds, the requirements that matter, and how to tell which apply to you.

item.title: India's IT Law, Explained: From the IT Act 2000 to the DPDP Era
item.description: A practitioner's map of India's IT law — the IT Act 2000, Sections 43 to 79, the struck-down 66A, the 2021 Rules, CERT-In directions, BNSS 94, and the DPDP Act.

item.title: How Cybercrime Cases Are Solved: From First Alert to the Courtroom
item.description: How a cybercrime case actually gets solved — incident response, the police investigation, digital forensics, chain of custody, and what makes electronic evidence stand in an Indian court.

item.title: Which AI Tool for Which Job: A Practitioner's Map
item.description: Chat, research, slides, images, video, meetings, code, automation — which AI tool fits each job, what the free tiers give you, and exactly where free stops.

item.title: I Open-Sourced My AI SDR
item.description: CleverResponder is my open-source AI SDR for SmartLead and Instantly: it classifies replies, drafts with AI, gets Slack approval, sends, and follows up.

item.title: Character Over Career: Five Choices I Live By
item.description: Character over career, satisfaction over success, failure over fear, people over place, goal over gossip — five choices that guide how I live and work.

item.title: My Career Story: From Classroom to AI
item.description: From a $6 mentoring session to published security research, 5,000+ interviews, and AI pipelines — my honest career story, setbacks included.

item.title: The Four M's Every Business Runs On
item.description: Manpower, money, mind, and management: what each pillar means, why businesses fail when one is missing, and how management binds the rest.

item.title: Lessons from Running an Internship Cohort
item.description: Why small cohorts beat crowds, hiring for hunger over resumes, giving real work instead of exercises, and why mentorship is mostly restraint.

item.title: How to Stand Out in an Internship Interview
item.description: Advice from 5,000+ interviews: why attitude beats aptitude, the homework nobody does, mistakes that sink candidates, and questions worth asking.

item.title: Smart Feedback: How to Give and Receive It
item.description: Why vague praise fails, a three-part structure for feedback that actually helps, and how to receive criticism without getting defensive.

item.title: How to Succeed in Software Development: The Four-Step Path
item.description: Make it work, make it modular, make it readable, then optimize. Why this order is the key to building software and automations that last.

item.title: What Is a Fork Bomb in Linux?
item.description: How one line of Bash can freeze a hardened Linux system, why ulimit and blacklists fall short, and the smarter defense from my research.

item.title: Automating Email Replies with n8n
item.description: How I build email reply automations with n8n: the five-stage workflow, where AI helps, guardrails that prevent bad sends, and mistakes to avoid.
